paper.title_en: Complex frequency evolution of direct waves from binary black hole mergers
paper.abstract_en: While no signal originating at a black hole's event horizon can reach future null infinity, information about the horizon and its immediate vicinity can be encoded in asymptotic properties of waves emitted by matter or field perturbations falling toward a growing/forming horizon. Within a response-filtered framework, "direct wave" denotes source-sensitive plunge and remnant-formation information revealed by filtering the black-hole response. Unlike a stationary damped sinusoid with a fixed complex frequency, the direct wave follows the evolving source and has an evolving instantaneous complex frequency tied at late times to the remnant horizon angular velocity $Ω_H$ and surface gravity $κ_H$. Using rational filters, we remove quasinormal modes from numerical-relativity waveforms to study this evolution. Before numerical contamination, trajectories depend on remnant spin: the real frequency evolves toward $2Ω_H$ from above for lower spins ($χ_f\lesssim0.7$) and from below for higher spins ($χ_f\gtrsim0.7$), while the instantaneous decay rate increases, with best-resolved cases approaching the expected value of $3κ_H$. As in particle-plunge results, the horizon-controlled value is approached only at late times, as frame dragging controls near-horizon motion. For $χ_f\sim0.7$ remnants of non-precessing, comparable-mass binaries, the early-time real frequency is close to $2Ω_H$ because the binary orbital frequency transitions smoothly to the remnant horizon frequency. Finite-time deviations therefore carry information about merger/collapse dynamics rather than undermining the horizon connection. Full direct-wave evolution requires numerical-relativity calibration. We further show that approximate pole-zero pairing in the Kerr response motivates a minimal filter set that suppresses quasinormal-mode features while revealing source-trajectory information.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 该文探讨双黑洞并合直波复频率演化，将晚期瞬时频率与视界角速度及表面引力联系起来，使用理性滤波从数值相对论波形中移除准正规模，方法清晰且问题位于广义相对论基础与黑洞物理交叉处；主题相关度高，理论深度与数值校准需求明确，值得点击阅读。
decision.title_zh: 双黑洞并合直波的复频率演化
decision.abstract_zh: 虽然任何起源于黑洞事件视界的信号都无法到达未来零无穷远，但关于视界及其紧邻区域的信息可以编码在由落入增长中/形成中视界的物质或场扰动所发射的波的渐近性质中。在响应滤波框架内，“直波”指通过滤波黑洞响应所揭示的对源敏感的 plunging 与遗迹形成信息。与具有固定复频率的稳态阻尼正弦波不同，直波跟随演化的源，并具有演化的瞬时复频率，在晚期与遗迹视界角速度 $Ω_H$ 和表面引力 $κ_H$ 相联系。使用理性滤波器，我们从数值相对论波形中移除准正规模以研究这种演化。在数值污染之前，轨迹依赖于遗迹自旋：实频率对于较低自旋（$χ_f\lesssim0.7$）从上方趋近 $2Ω_H$，对于较高自旋（$χ_f\gtrsim0.7$）从下方趋近 $2Ω_H$，而瞬时衰减率增加，其中分辨最好的情形接近期望值 $3κ_H$。如同粒子 plunging 结果，仅在晚期才趋近视界控制的值，因为参考系拖曳控制近视界运动。对于非进动、等质量双星的 $χ_f\sim0.7$ 遗迹，早期实频率接近 $2Ω_H$，因为双星轨道频率平滑过渡到遗迹视界频率。因此有限时间偏差携带的是关于并合/坍缩动力学而非破坏视界联系的信息。完整的直波演化需要数值相对论校准。我们进一步表明，Kerr 响应中的近似极点-零点配对促成了一个最小滤波器集，该滤波器集抑制准正规模特征，同时揭示源轨迹信息。
